body:
You are drafting spoken lines for a video game. Reply with plain text only, in the exact row format given at the end of this message. Do not send messages to anyone else and do not ask questions: decide. Write nothing but the rows (no title, no notes, no Markdown).

THE GAME. "The Crooked Moon" is a single-player, turn-based tactical party RPG built from a folk-horror Dungeons and Dragons campaign. It is set in Wickermoor Hollow, a haunted valley in Druskenvald, a land of endless night under a giant Crooked Moon with a crone's face. The look is a Halloween that never ends, drawn like an 1980s cartoon. A ghost train, the Ghostlight Express, has crashed in the valley; the party is stranded in the Hollow and its village, Wickermoor. The tone is warm, wry and funny on the surface, with real dread and real grief underneath. The player controls a party of four chosen from six companions: Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward, Silas Vane, Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein. They are quirky, capable adults.

THE NARRATOR. A NARRATOR row is spoken by the Vagrant, the green-skinned ferryman of the ghost train, who tells the tale in a folksy Southern drawl. At the camp fire he is warm and wry, and when a talk turns sad his humour leaves and he goes plain and level. He speaks to the party as "you" and about the companion in the third person, by first name. Present tense, one or two sentences, under about 32 words. Concrete senses (a smell, a sound, a touch, what the hands are doing) over adjectives. Never tell the player what to feel. Never "suddenly". No facts the party could not see. Drop the final g ("hangin'") in about one Narrator row in four, and use no other dialect spelling. He is kind, never mocks a stumble and never makes light of the dead.

RULES FOR EVERY LINE.
1. The companion's voice sheet below comes first. Match its accent, pace, vocabulary and contractions, and the existing lines. Use a pet phrase at most twice in the whole reply and never twice in one talk. Never repeat or closely paraphrase a line already in the voice sheet or the note.
2. A SAY row is the companion speaking: one or two short sentences, under about 28 words. Never put three sentences in one row; start another row instead.
3. The party's options (OPTION rows) are under 12 words, in the plain voice of the party, work at any hour and in any weather, never name a hero, and are never rolls or checks. A reply must always answer the option it follows.
4. Canon limits. Use only the facts in the voice sheet and the note below. Do not invent a new named person, place, monster, event, object the companion carries, or piece of the companion's history. You may invent small, harmless habits, fondnesses, superstitions and turns of phrase, and the look of the fire and the night. Name no place that the note does not name. Never state a dark secret. You may come close to one and step back.
5. Nothing here is a game system: no dice, no checks, no points, no levels, no HP, no "approval", no menus talked about aloud. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks inside a line when someone is quoted). No em dashes, no semicolons, no brackets, no asterisks, no stage directions, no placeholders.
6. Humour comes from the character, never explained. The sad turn is plain and short.
7. Our own words. Nothing quoted from any book.

THIS REQUEST. Region banter for Skitterdeep Mine: 7 short exchanges between two or three companions, spoken as the party walks about this place. There are no Narrator rows, no options and no replies. Every row is a companion talking to another companion, never to the player.

HOW IT WORKS. When the party comes into an area, now and then one exchange plays as a few lines of chat between companions who happen to be in the party, once each. Only two or three of the six are ever in the party, so each exchange stands alone, mentions nobody else and needs no setup. Each one below is about what is in front of the party in one place at one moment of the story. Banter is funny first; one line in an exchange may turn honest, never more. The chat is about the place: what it looks and smells like, what is odd or sad or silly in it, and how each companion's trade, habits and fears meet it.

RULES.
1. Each exchange is 4 to 6 SAY rows, each a companion's single line (one or two short sentences, under about 28 words), alternating naturally between the speakers; every speaker listed speaks at least once.
2. Use only the facts in the attached cast sheets and the "In front of them" facts of that exchange. The "Story now" line is everything the party knows of the story: a remark must never run ahead of it (name a villain, a fight or a result only if the Story now line does). Never state or hint at any companion's past or secret, and never say what anyone's debt is. No new named people, places or monsters.
3. Pet words and phrases: each companion's at most once in an exchange, and never in two consecutive lines. Companions call each other by first name.
4. No two exchanges may share a joke or a topic, and no line may repeat a line in a cast sheet. Spread the topics: do not make every exchange about the same kind of thing.
5. Plain punctuation only (commas, full stops, hyphens, apostrophes, question marks, quotation marks). No em dashes, semicolons, brackets, asterisks or stage directions. No game terms. Our own words.
AVOID in this region: What Tobin tastes in the ground at the end of his chapter is his own scene: nobody tastes the earth or names a root. Tobin and Silas's plague-tonic scene is theirs: do not stage it. Do not describe Stonoga or what is in the deep level.

THE EXCHANGES (in this order):
EXCHANGE 1: Silas + Lucan (speaker ids: silas_vane, lucan_houndstooth)
  Story now: The party is on the rutted hill trail north-west of the village, on its way to the mine. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Hill Trail: A rutted trail through wooded hills north-west of Wickermoor, with a clearing where it bends. The trail climbs through wet beech and hornbeam. Mist lies in the hollows and the ruts are full of tiny crawling things. Parts of it: The west trail; The clearing at the bend; The east trail. Things to see: A rotted saddle bag in the brambles; A hunters' cairn; A fallen log; Tiny centipedes crossing the ruts; Tiny centipedes, all heading the same way.
EXCHANGE 2: Rook + Tobin (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, tobin_hayward)
  Story now: The party has come to the abandoned mining camp, with the headframe over its black shaft.
  Talk about: its first look: what the party sees and smells on coming in.
  In front of them: Glitterdeep Mine: An abandoned mining camp in a ridge of wooded hills, with a headframe over a black shaft and a sign with two letters painted over. The camp is sagging timber, rust and rail. A headframe stands over a square hole that breathes green gas, and the sign over the warehouse says Skitterdeep. Parts of it: The shaft head; The old drift's mouth; The warehouse yard; The camp road; The kennel yard. Things to see: The warehouse sign; The camp, and the headframe beyond; The headframe over the shaft; The beam and the hanging chain; Green gas, rising; Old maintenance rungs in the shaft wall; An old kennel with a numbered brass collar; A flat stone at the camp's edge; An ore cart, on its side.
EXCHANGE 3: Delphine + Cordelia (speaker ids: delphine_ravelle, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party is in the upper workings, below the headframe.
  In front of them: The Upper Workings: The old drift, the lift landing 30 feet down the shaft, and the Crosscut. Rotten timbering, overturned minecarts, and a smell of old meat rising from far below. Parts of it: The old drift; The diggers' cavern; The drift, east; The lift landing; The Crosscut; The hoard chamber. Things to see: The lift: planks over three iron beams; Old maintenance rungs; Working tools along the drift; An eye hanging by its nerve; A heap of gold and gems; Silver chalices and silks; A scatter of jewels; Coins by the handful; A heap of organs.
EXCHANGE 4: Lucan + Cordelia (speaker ids: lucan_houndstooth, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come into the machine shop, where the middle room smells of horse and rot. Lucan's hound may be called Barnaby now and is known to fear thunder.
  In front of them: The Machine Shop: A rusted shop of three rooms; the middle one smells of horse and rot. Warped boards leak green gas. Three rooms, two doors between them, and handprints in the dust. Parts of it: Tool storage; The fleshdobbins' lair; The winch house; The machine shop. Things to see: Handprints in the dust; A maul under a tarp; A dungeoneer's pack, half buried; A rack of ruined tools; A rubbish-pile bed under a horse blanket; A rubbish-pile bed under a wine-red surcoat; A rubbish-pile bed; Rotted wine-red surcoats; The winch drum and its lever box. People here: The parcel rider.
EXCHANGE 5: Silas + Cordelia (speaker ids: silas_vane, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has come into the mine's old store.
  In front of them: The Warehouse: The mine's old store, smashed and sleeping. Broken shelves, rubble to the ankle, a thin green haze and the sound of heavy breathing. Parts of it: The warehouse floor; The sleepers. Things to see: A pallet of rusted sheet metal; A heap of miners' leavings; A rotted lunch pail; A foreman's board, half legible; Rubble and old crates; A barrel of rotted flour; Tiny centipedes in the flour; Cobwebs.
EXCHANGE 6: Rook + Cordelia (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, cordelia_skein)
  Story now: The party has gone down to the deep level.
  In front of them: The Deep Level: The Deep Drift with its sigils, and Stonoga's laboratory. Yellow-green haze, walls that squirm when you look at them, and a bronze door lit by a slow green-purple pulse. Parts of it: The sigil chamber; The Deep Drift; The shaft's foot; The bronze door; Stonoga's laboratory. Things to see: The bottom of the shaft; The yellow-green haze; The haze, thicker here; A ring of knotted entrails, sweating gas; Sinew knotted into the floor; A wall of soft, slick flesh; Tiny centipedes, thick as spilled rice; Water trickling somewhere in the dark; The laboratory.
EXCHANGE 7: Rook + Silas (speaker ids: rook_coldwake, silas_vane)
  Story now: Stonoga is dead. The party is back at the camp above the shaft.
  Talk about: something different from the other exchange in this place: how it feels now.
  In front of them: Glitterdeep Mine: An abandoned mining camp in a ridge of wooded hills, with a headframe over a black shaft and a sign with two letters painted over. The camp is sagging timber, rust and rail. A headframe stands over a square hole that breathes green gas, and the sign over the warehouse says Skitterdeep. Parts of it: The shaft head; The old drift's mouth; The warehouse yard; The camp road; The kennel yard. Things to see: The warehouse sign; The camp, and the headframe beyond; The headframe over the shaft; The beam and the hanging chain; Green gas, rising; Old maintenance rungs in the shaft wall; An old kennel with a numbered brass collar; A flat stone at the camp's edge; An ore cart, on its side.

THE ROW FORMAT (exact). One row per line:

EXCHANGE <number>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
SAY <speaker id>: <line>
...

Use the speaker ids exactly as given (for example SAY rook_coldwake: ...). Write exactly 7 EXCHANGE blocks, numbered 1 to 7, and nothing else.

ATTACHED DOCUMENTS. Two documents come attached to this message; read both before you write: `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-1.md` (the voice sheets and fact lists for Rook Coldwake, Tobin Hayward and Silas Vane) and `tasks/crooked-moon-companions/banter-cast-2.md` (the same for Delphine Ravelle, Lucan Houndstooth and Cordelia Skein).
result:
EXCHANGE 1
SAY silas_vane: Look at the ruts under the hornbeam, Lucan, every tiny centipede in the mud is marching one way like the house just called last bets.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: A disciplined column, Silas, though I can only award them a four out of ten for spoor discipline across a wet wagon track.
SAY silas_vane: Your little Barnaby isn't grading them, friend, he's eyeing that rotted saddle bag in the brambles like it owes him cheese.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Hush now, the dark has teeth under these beeches, and a gentleman's hound does not rummage through unclaimed luggage.
SAY silas_vane: Tell's in the twitch, friend, and right now my ribs say whatever called those crawlers uphill is holding a stacked shoe.
EXCHANGE 2
SAY rook_coldwake: Unfenced square shaft, sagging headframe timber, and green gas rising straight into the yard without a vent flue. Shocking neglect of parish code, Tobin.
SAY tobin_hayward: Never mind the timber, Rook, someone painted Skitterdeep right over Glitterdeep on that warehouse sign, and bad naming is how rot gets a taproot.
SAY rook_coldwake: Painting over two letters without filing a variance is a municipal offence, and leaving a tipped ore cart in the road is another.
SAY tobin_hayward: Keep that turnip lantern steady by the drift mouth, the green damp coming up those iron rungs smells like a cellar that forgot how to drain.
SAY rook_coldwake: Settle down now, I will log the rusted hanging chain on the docket, provided you remind me to draw breath before we climb down.
EXCHANGE 3
SAY delphine_ravelle: Rotten timbering, overturned carts, and a heap of gold and gems sitting twenty paces from a pile of loose organs. Terrible staging, Cordelia, no sense of billing.
SAY cordelia_skein: On the contrary, Delphine, the eye hanging by its optic nerve over the Crosscut shows a remarkably steady hand with tissue suspension.
SAY delphine_ravelle: He says the silver chalices are tarnished on the bias, darling, and frankly the smell of old meat coming up the lift shaft is ruining my velvet.
SAY cordelia_skein: Fascinating pathology, though, how the humidity from thirty feet down preserves the humours while the silks beside the coins are already spotting with mould.
SAY delphine_ravelle: Mind the seams, darling, and do not touch a single jewel until we know who left their liver in the cheap seats.
EXCHANGE 4
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Good heavens, Cordelia, this middle room smells of dead horse and sour grease, and someone has made a bed out of rotted wine-red surcoats.
SAY cordelia_skein: Look at the dust by the winch drum, Lucan, the handprints between the two doors have a most irregular span across the knuckles.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Sloppy posture on the approach, if you please, and they left a perfectly serviceable maul under a tarp while burying a dungeoneer's pack in rubbish.
SAY cordelia_skein: The green gas leaking through the warped boards is coating the ruined tools on the rack, darling, I would love to assay a scraping.
SAY lucan_houndstooth: Take your specimen quickly, then, for Barnaby has flattened his ears at that horse blanket, and I do not care for how my own throat is rumbling.
EXCHANGE 5
SAY silas_vane: Smashed shelves, rubble to the ankle, and somebody's still snoring in the green haze like they paid rent on the floor. Bad odds in this store, Cordelia.
SAY cordelia_skein: Notice the barrel of rotted flour by the crates, Silas, the tiny centipedes have colonized the meal at an admirably uniform ratio.
SAY silas_vane: Yeah, well, they can keep the flour and the rusted sheet metal, I'm reading the chalk on this half-legible foreman's board to see who's still on the tab.
SAY cordelia_skein: Do hold still by that rotted lunch pail, darling, your smaller shadow is lagging a full step behind you in the cobwebs.
SAY silas_vane: Leave the shade alone, friend, when you hear heavy breathing in a wrecked room and nobody wakes up, you keep your bone cards palmed.
EXCHANGE 6
SAY rook_coldwake: Sinew knotted into the floor slabs and a ring of entrails sweating yellow-green gas across the thoroughfare. There is no zoning in the north that permits a wall of slick flesh, Cordelia.
SAY cordelia_skein: All six of my eyes just clicked at once, Rook, the vascular calibration holding that bronze door to the living tissue is exquisite.
SAY rook_coldwake: The wall squirmed when I checked the plumb line, and the centipedes are thick as spilled rice around the foot of the shaft.
SAY cordelia_skein: Hear the water trickling in the dark behind the green-purple pulse, darling, the whole drift is circulating like an opened thorax.
SAY rook_coldwake: Mind the turf by those sigils, then, my knuckles are going soft enough in this damp without stepping in an unlicensed laboratory.
EXCHANGE 7
SAY silas_vane: Funny how a place looks when the bank's broken, Rook, same sagging timber and rusted rail, but the chill in my ribs finally folded its hand.
SAY rook_coldwake: The square shaft is still breathing green gas into the yard, Silas, though the draught coming off the ridge has lost its grease.
SAY silas_vane: Look at the kennel yard there, an old doghouse and a numbered brass collar in the weeds, and nobody left to whistle at the end of the shift.
SAY rook_coldwake: Numbered brass is proper parish registry, at least, better than leaving a watchman's name to wash off the warehouse sign.
SAY silas_vane: Come on, sit on that flat stone at the camp's edge and take a breath for the shift log, friend, we cleared the table.
